extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit grant writers and organizations seeking funding (community programs, program directors, grant coordinators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing competitive grant proposals for nonprofit/community programs, covering problem statements, objectives, methodology, evaluation, budgets, matching shares, cash flow, future funding, and appendices. Aimed at organizations preparing proposals to foundations, government, or corporate funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkages and licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe linkages with other organizations involved in the field and inform the funding agency of any licenses obtained to provide the proposed or established service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show collaborations and formal agreements; list licenses relevant to service delivery. Demonstrates community connections and legal readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clients (proof of satisfied clients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that you have satisfied clients by including written statements or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include testimonials, reference letters, or client satisfaction statements to demonstrate credibility and prior success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteers (motivation and retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe why your volunteers like doing what they do for your organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain volunteer incentives, roles, satisfaction, and how volunteer engagement supports the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities (location advantages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how your location benefits your task geographically and demographically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain accessibility, demographic fit, proximity to target population, and facility suitability for proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what your organization has done in the past that will aid it in reaching its new goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize relevant prior projects, outcomes, and lessons learned that increase funder confidence in capacity to deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that you have handled budgets successfully in the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prior audit reports, financial statements, examples of on-budget project management to demonstrate stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior funding (demonstration of external support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a few examples of other funders that have shown faith in your capabilities; private funding usually leads to public funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List previous funders, grant amounts, and project outcomes as evidence of fundability and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need (evidence of real need)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that there is a real need that must be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local and comparative statistical data to demonstrate scope; avoid overwhelming reviewers with data; prioritize local sources and use national data only for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement (focus and realism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the problem or situation in your target area that needs addressing, relate it to the overall environment and its impact if not rectified, and focus on constituency needs rather than organizational concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific but avoid exaggeration; explain the condition causing the problem; include statistics, know constituency desires, describe other experts' work and linkages; present a single optimal solution rather than multiple options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (measurable, client-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific components of your overall goal in measurable, quantifiable terms from the client's point of view; objectives should be terminal (describe end-state at project conclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure objectives tie problem description to services provided; use objectives to focus activity and provide benchmarks for achievement; avoid confusing objectives with activities or broad goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective types (input, process, impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize three categories of objectives: program inputs (resources/quantities), program process (services delivered), and impact/output objectives (lasting benefits after participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: increase number of training sites (input); provide X units of service (process); reduce dependency or increase employment (impact). Use appropriate category when designing objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective components (what/who/where/when/extent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write objectives including five essential parts: What (action verb), Who (target group), Where (location), When (target date or schedule), and What extent (measure for evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these components to make objectives specific and evaluable; these form the basis for product evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (detailed methods and justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods/strategies/activities/procedures to accomplish objectives, including what you're doing, justification, flow of activities and timing, target population characteristics and selection, staff requirements, and start-up activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how methodology flows from objectives; include timetable; be explicit about who does what and why; avoid vague descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology design elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include design specifics such as the basic technique/approach (case study, pilot, controlled experiment), population recruitment and role in planning, treatment/procedures in sufficient detail, reporting and participant tracking, management structure, and time schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough procedural detail that reviewers understand implementation; include sample instruments in appendix; consider charts for timelines if cogent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities (chronological tasks and backward chaining)
rubrics_metrics.description: List activities as chronological steps required to accomplish strategies/objectives; develop activities by 'backward chaining' from the final step to the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backward chaining helps ensure all steps are listed and detailed; include time and resource estimates for each activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (purpose and components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how data will be collected, progress monitored and analyzed; types of evaluation (product and/or process); recordkeeping; evaluator's identity/credentials/impartiality; reporting procedures; and specific due dates for evaluation tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders want measurable indicators before, during, and after the program. Specify instruments, schedules, who collects data, and how results will inform program modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product evaluation (goal/objective achievement measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Product evaluation measures success in meeting objectives — did you meet projected statistics and were clients better off?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantifiable measures (reduced costs per participant, increased placements, percent placed in unsubsidized jobs, etc.) to demonstrate outcomes and cost-efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process evaluation (methods and cost-effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process evaluation measures the methods used to work toward goals, examining whether benefits were worth implementation costs and whether each step met higher goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare planned vs actual processes, assess efficiency, and use findings to improve program operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate post-program success measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure short-term outcomes seen from client's history, such as increased employment, earnings, labor force participation, reduced dependency, mobility, and placements in jobs/geographic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples and numeric targets (e.g., number of registrants entering employment, increased average hourly wage) to show expected immediate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program operating efficiency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include measures that directly observe project functions to judge efficiency (workload, capacity for work, complexity/mix of activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: increase intake by X percent to Y total; increase tests administered to a target number. Use these to assess how well activities were performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget (clear, supported, and concise)
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicitly what money is needed; ensure proposal supports each item in the budget; provide budget summary and detailed justification with totals broken into requested amount, organization contribution, and other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep budget concise (excessive length suggests poor organization). Support each line item and do not inflate costs; many funders will fund to the penny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and wages (detailed line item)
rubrics_metrics.description: List each staff position with title, salary ranges, number of persons, months/weeks devoted to project, percent time on project, and total salaries per position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about staffing cost calculations; link staff roles to methodology and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits (explicit rates and computation)
rubrics_metrics.description: List fringe benefits for project staff (FICA, unemployment, workers' compensation, hospitalization), and include computation and rate details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide calculation methods and justification for fringe rates used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant and contractual services
rubrics_metrics.description: Include procurement contracts, agreements with affiliates/cooperating institutions, and all consultant costs; list fees for legal, accounting and professional services with specific cost breakouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify scope of work for consultants and justify costs; ensure items are not duplicated across lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space costs (rent, utilities, maintenance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document payments for rent, utilities, janitorial services, maintenance, and necessary alterations; if housed within your facility, a cost analysis may be required to determine rent charged to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show monthly space cost multiplied by project months or cost per square foot; check funder policies for allowed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment purchases and rentals
rubrics_metrics.description: Define equipment purchases (non-expendable items with useful life >1 year and unit cost ≥ $300) and include transportation/installation costs; list rental costs separately and check funder limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify funder policies on equipment purchase vs rental; specify each equipment item and cost; include lease-purchase options if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumable supplies and utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include office and program supplies (paper, pens, etc.) and, if appropriate, separate utilities (electricity, gas) as budget items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out consumables by category if needed; follow any provided budget format or funder instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel (purpose, mileage, allowable rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: List transportation, meals and lodging of staff in accordance with funder's policy; project local mileage and specify purpose for each staff position; check allowable rates for in-state/out-of-state travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify travel as program-related (training, conferences); obtain funder pre-approval if required for out-of-state travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommunications
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget for installation and monthly charges for telephone lines, computer phone lines, fax machines, mobile phones, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include necessary telecommunications for program delivery and administration; itemize monthly and one-time costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income (treatment and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for direct charges or fees to participants; program income must be kept in a restricted account and either returned to the granting agency or used to fund direct costs expanding services; may not be used as match with some funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funder rules on program income use and carryover; never treat program income as matching share unless allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special project costs and other costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include project-specific costs (meals for children, training manuals, printing) and other items such as maintenance, postage, repair charges, meeting costs, subscriptions, temporary help, insurance and bonding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific cost breakouts for each listed special or other cost item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhead/indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify administrative costs determined by charging a fixed percentage of the total grant request; ensure these costs don't duplicate other line items and check funder allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some funders disallow indirect cost charges or require approved cost allocation plans for government grants; state the indirect cost rate and basis, and avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching share (cash and in-kind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the portion of project costs not borne by the funding source; may include grantee charges, cash contributions from others, and services/property donated (in-kind).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List examples of allowable cash match (salaries, travel, supplies) and in-kind (use of depreciable equipment, donated services, office space). Check funder rules; ensure valuations reflect fair market value and do not exceed comparable value at time of donation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of volunteer and donated services
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer services may be counted as in-kind match if integral to approved plan; rates should be consistent with similar work payments or market rates when skills are not found in the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an employer furnishes an employee, value services at the employee's regular rate (excluding fringe/overhead). For donated expendable property, value should not exceed fair market value at donation time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of donated nonexpendable property and space
rubrics_metrics.description: Value donated equipment/buildings/land per purpose of grant: full value may be claimed if grant furnishes facility, or depreciation/use charges if used part-time; value cannot exceed fair market value and donated space cannot exceed fair rental value (independent appraisal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply appropriate valuation method (full value vs depreciation) based on grant purpose; document appraisals and basis for valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Address relationship between organization's disbursement needs and the funder's reimbursement process, and maintain a monthly measure of actual versus planned expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for reimbursement-only systems (vouchers) vs advance payments; gauge cash needs for startup and monthly periods; prepare and submit vouchers timely; monitor each line item to avoid overruns or idle funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget presentation cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid excessive length in the budget section and do not inflate the budget because funders typically fund exactly what is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, clear budget demonstrates organization; provide justified, realistic costs tied to program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future funding and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Show plans for future funding: potential for spin-off, whether you'll seek future funding from same/other sources, implications if outside support declines, and whether the organization can operate the project without outside funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate next-year operating costs by analyzing past line-item costs and considering inflation, pay increases, retirement/fringe changes, legal/regulatory changes, and variations in rent/insurance/audit/postage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix items (required supporting documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include supporting documents such as 501(c)(3) tax exemption letter, board member list with contacts, most recent audit and financial statements, annual report, resumes of key project staff, letters of support, news clippings, and organizational brochures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package appendix materials neatly and orderly; number and label each appendix and refer to appendix numbers in the body of the proposal to ease reviewer review.
